title: Fix Quality and Outliers: Weighing a Fix by What the Receiver Says It Is, Refusing One That Is Too Far From Where the Robot Is, and Taking One Back After Too Many Refusals

questions.question: What information is in a GNSS fix besides the position?
options: The level of the fix, which says how much to believe it
questions.explanation: A fixed fix is good to centimetres, a float to a quarter of a metre and a single to a metre and a half. The level is how the receiver says which.

questions.question: On the single fixes the filter that weighed them had an rms error of:
questions.explanation: Given the 1.5 m noise that a single fix has, the filter smoothed them to 0.67 m. Taking each as good to 2 cm, it followed the noise: 2.81 m.

questions.question: The worst error with the gate was:
questions.explanation: Five fixes were thrown 8 m. The filter that took them all was pulled 6.04 m off; the gate refused them, and what was left was the noise of single fixes.

questions.question: The gate refused what share of the good fixes?
options: 0.2 percent, near the 1 percent its threshold says
questions.explanation: The gate is the 99 percent point of a chi-square with two degrees of freedom, so about one correct fix in a hundred is expected to be refused. Here it was 0.2 percent.

questions.question: Why did a gate that never gives up find a carried robot so late?
options: The gate was set too loose
Every fix was refused until the filter's uncertainty had grown to admit 20 m
questions.explanation: The gate assumes the filter is right. Carried 20 m, the robot refused 68 fixes, 14 s of them, while it believed it was somewhere else.

questions.question: What does max_refused do?
options: Limits how many fixes are refused in a run
Raises the gate after each refusal
Switches the receiver to single level
After that many refusals in a row, the next fix is taken as a new start
questions.explanation: With a limit of 5 the carried robot was found five fixes after it was put down. The risk is that five bad fixes in a row can do the same.
